title: Four-Chilli Cheeseburgers
changes_from_base: Four kinds of chilli: charred and peeled poblanos, pickled jalapeños, chipotle-adobo mayonnaise and pepper Jack cheese, on larger patties grilled over high heat.
summary: Juicy beef layered with three types of chilli—roasted poblanos, pickled jalapeños and fiery chipotle mayo—all balanced by creamy pepper Jack cheese.
equipment: barbecue (or griddle pan and gas flame)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
chipotle chilli in adobo, finely chopped, plus 2 tsp of the sauce

steps.title: Mayo
steps.text: Stir 1 finely chopped chipotle chilli in adobo (plus 2 tsp of the sauce) and 4 tbsp mayonnaise together.

steps.title: Poblanos
steps.text: Char 2 fresh poblano chillies over the hot coals or a gas flame, turning, until blistered all over; wrap in foil for 5 min, then peel off most of the skin, discard stalks and seeds and chop roughly.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Divide 900 g beef chuck mince into 4 and shape patties about 1 cm wider than the buns, season well.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill the patties over the hot side turning now and then for about 8-10 min until well charred and 71 °C in the centre; top each with 2 slices of pepper Jack cheese, move to a plate and cover with foil.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Toast 4 large burger buns on the hot side for about 30 s.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Place patties on bun bases, then 30 g pickled jalapeño slices and the poblanos, top with chipotle mayo, close and serve.

tips: Char poblanos directly over a flame or coals until skin is completely blistered for easy peeling.
Shape the patties about 1 cm wider than the buns; they shrink as they grill.
Make the chipotle mayo up to 2 days ahead; chill until ready.
safety: Wash hands thoroughly after handling chillies to avoid capsaicin transferring to your eyes.
storage: Keep cooked patties for 2 days in the fridge; store the roasted poblano mixture and chipotle mayo separately for 3-4 days. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
